markdown: ## Watchlist - **Carrier:** It has released an enhanced building automation system (BAS) designed to simplify building operations [ACHR News](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMipAFBVV95cUxQTDVaOHBlTTdmWFZ0UzhoQ2RhV3JtZ2djUGZKVktNSDgyR1dTR2hSdFZpSXFCUG1fcFZTVUEzaXV0OUNXSUFUN25hUXZwOVQzMnRmUWxreU9QbV8zTDNxQzMyOTdlLW1FQ0xmbmxHbnlab2xfS3N5Z3FjLS1keHYwZkFxTHpmNFFhYlhOU3VtbXVwZ1dxa1RVZmpSakJmNTYybk40dg?oc=5). That strengthens the controls and services side of the business, which tends to carry recurring revenue. - **JPMorgan:** Card chief Allison Beer is leaving for an "external opportunity" [Bloomberg.com](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMixwFBVV95cUxNRnhKbDF3M1M0UFViWFRTYU9XbHMwaENVT0ltamdqazZFX2NPYWxxMDdiX28tV3NoR0RuaGZVUEM0Nmg0TDZBdGQyM2gwWkY0MkJteGM4Q3BtcHU1bkFtOUpMQmVSYXcwV1FEYzVNVll6ZkNTdHB0NS1MQ2lmbE1VcWgwQm1jMlBRcUtsLVdhNkgwYjZHamNEbU5mUFk4ZWZZZC1xc1RiQnA1UURYQ3ZVZmZjYXp4SUU2RjF3N2luVkZ4emZrNk9N?oc=5). This is a leadership change in consumer cards, so expect no direct impact on corporate treasury coverage. ## The brief - **US producer prices are rising at a 6.5% annual pace, and Fed officials are signalling a hike** [CFO Dive](https://www.cfodive.com/news/producer-prices-surge-annual-pace-fed-officials-signal-hike-federal-reserve/874687/). Daly says the Fed will "in all likelihood" raise rates, and Goolsbee says it "has definitely got work to do" [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/13/chicago-feds-goolsbee-says-central-bank-has-definitely-got-work-to-do-on-inflation.html). Plan for higher USD floating costs and keep dollar cash short until the path is clearer. - **Markets are still pricing in two more ECB rate hikes** [The Irish Times](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMinAFBVV95cUxPdEZob0xWLTJNSVJ1cXpQbUxSb25ob0VLd3lQVFNvaDVmRUhMTlZGT2pfdmk0NGN3OFdJaHFUVnRVamFCY0gwN0xoQUVIeXpXTHR0MkpMdW5rM1B6ZnVaMzBDTUhIVFFVR21GeW5jN012d1lfa3kzaUUxLUoxcnBOVEt3VUtEQng2WWswS0lianNQejhucW1ybTczRFA?oc=5). Euro deposit yields should keep rising for now, so stagger euro placements rather than locking in long tenors. - **The Bank of England, the Monetary Authority of Singapore and the Bank of Thailand have launched Project Meridian FX APAC** [Bank of England](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/news/2026/november/the-boe-monetary-authority-of-singapore-and-bank-of-thailand-media-release). The details are thin, but central-bank work on FX infrastructure in Asia-Pacific is worth tracking for how intercompany flows in the region get settled. - **China's slowdown deepened in October, with industrial output, retail sales and investment all missing estimates** [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/16/china-retail-sales-october-industrial-output-investment.html). Weaker domestic demand in China is a risk to local revenue and receivables, and it leaves the economy more exposed to shocks abroad. ## Rates & FX - **Treasuries had their worst week since Trump's "liberation day"** [Financial Times](https://www.ft.com/content/7bebace2-dc87-410a-ae29-ffd9f3176def?syn-25a6b1a6=1). The 10-year is 5.15% (+29bp on the week) and the 2-year is 4.88% (+37bp). SOFR is 3.90%. Term funding above 5% now looks like the base case, not a spike. - **The dollar strengthened again.** EUR/USD is 1.1052 (-1.01% on the week) and GBP/USD is 1.3227 (-1.18%). USD/JPY is 160.00, up 1.06% on the week and at a level that could invite intervention risk. USD/MXN fell 0.52% to 18.593, so the peso firmed. USD/CNY is 6.6719 and EUR/GBP is 0.8356. - **€STR is 2.443% and SONIA is 3.9845%.** Both are unchanged, with SONIA's 25bp step now fully in the data. - **Fed Chairman Warsh speaks today at 17:00 Dublin.** A hawkish message would back a December hike and the dollar. Later this week: US retail sales on Tuesday, UK CPI and the FOMC minutes on Wednesday, and China's loan prime rates on Friday. ## Also worth knowing - **An S&P report warns that European banks' growing use of significant risk transfers (SRTs) raises their exposure to "forced deleveraging"** [Financial Times](https://www.ft.com/content/3b6cccb1-cac2-4e64-a2c2-3b3801f9a5fb?syn-25a6b1a6=1). - **PayPal wants its own bank**, both to lend to merchants and to diversify its sources of capital [Payments Dive](https://www.paymentsdive.com/news/why-paypal-wants-to-have-a-bank/874615/). - **BASF has opened a $1bn MDI production plant in Louisiana**, its largest single US investment to date [Manufacturing Dive](https://www.manufacturingdive.com/news/basf-verbund-mdi-facility-polyurethanes-geismar-louisiana/874549/). - **Ireland's climate plan for more than 700,000 homes faces a clash with the fuel industry over delays and low ambition** [Irish Independent](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMi-?oc=5). ## Worth thinking about HBR argues the market is mispricing resilience, calling it an increasingly important and underpriced growth asset [HBR](/2026/11/the-market-is-mispricing-resilience). With term rates above 5% and the dollar rising, it is worth asking whether Carrier's liquidity buffers, hedge programme and supplier finance are valued in capital allocation as resilience, or treated only as costs.
